nv_north_face_3.blurb: A big sandstone wall on the shady side of Whiskey Peak, up Black Velvet Canyon in Red Rock Canyon west of Las Vegas. Nearly every one of the 29 climbs is trad, with just a couple of bolted lines, and many are long multi-pitch outings rather than quick laps. Grades start around 5.8 and reach 5.12, with the weight of the wall sitting in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, so it suits confident leaders more than newcomers. Expect a committing day: a real walk up a cairned trail, a full rack, and time to descend. The most popular lines see a steady stream of parties, while the rest of the wall is quieter.

nv_classic_rock_wall.blurb: A newer, mostly bolted face in the Calico Basin part of Red Rock Canyon, a short stroll from the first pullout lot on the scenic loop. Of its 29 climbs, 26 are sport, with a pair of trad lines and a single top-rope. The grades span 5.6 up to 5.13, but the bulk sit between 5.8 and 5.11, with a healthy number of 5.10s and 5.11s, so it works for a mixed group. Climbing runs from slabby and technical to steeper and pumpy, with huecos on some lines. The base is open and roomy, and the canyon walls cut most of the wind.

nv_1_sandy_cove_area.blurb: The leftmost wall in Rainbow Canyon, a remote tuff canyon in Lincoln County, south of Caliente in eastern Nevada. It holds 28 climbs split fairly evenly between bolted sport lines and traditional routes, from about 5.7 up to 5.12. Most of the grades fall at 5.9 and 5.10, with a smaller group of 5.11s, which makes it a good fit for solid intermediate climbers. The rock is clean tuff with cracks, corners and bolted faces. This is a far-flung spot with no services, so come stocked with food, water and a full tank.

nv_monkey_bar_boulder.blurb: One of the best-known blocks at Kraft Boulders, in the east cluster of the Calico Basin side of Red Rock Canyon. All 28 problems here are bouldering, and the spread is wide: a few at V0 and V1, a solid core around V2 and V3, then a run of harder lines from V5 up through the double digits, topping out near V12. That range means a mixed group can all find something to try on one rock. The boulder is reached by a walk of roughly twenty minutes on the Kraft Mountain Loop trail, which splits to pass either side of it.

nv_black_velvet_wall.blurb: A towering sandstone face in Black Velvet Canyon, Red Rock Canyon, and one of the park's marquee trad destinations. Of 28 climbs, 27 are trad and one is sport, with nearly all graded between 5.9 and 5.12 and the largest cluster at 5.10. Routes run from four pitches to well over a dozen, and styles range from chimneys to thin balancy edges. The wall is shaded for much of the day. Reaching it takes a wash walk, a short third-class scramble and some contouring, and the walk-off means a long outing: bring a rack, two ropes on some lines, water and a plan for the descent.

nv_rattlsnake_crag.blurb: A low, south-facing cliff in the McCullough Hills above Henderson, near Las Vegas, standing around 35 feet at its highest. Among its 28 climbs are a good number of boulder problems, about ten trad lines, a few sport routes and a couple of top-ropes. Boulders run from V0 to V3, and the roped climbs from roughly 5.7 to 5.11. It is an easy half-day stop rather than a destination, with the cliff visible from the trailhead. The rock quality varies, and the top edge is loose, so set up anchors with care and back from the lip.

nv_ragged_edges_area.blurb: A crack-heavy sandstone wall in the Willow Spring zone of Red Rock Canyon, off the paved loop road west of Las Vegas. Of 28 climbs, 27 are trad and one is sport. The grades start at 5.5 and climb to 5.11, with a friendly cluster in the 5.6 to 5.8 range, plus a decent set of 5.10s and 5.11s, so it serves beginners learning to place gear as well as stronger leaders. Walk-ins are short and gentle. A famous two-pitch moderate crack here draws most of the traffic, and parking in the surrounding Willow Spring lots can fill on pleasant weekends.

nv_kraft_crags.blurb: A low cliff band on the sunny south side of Kraft Mountain, in Calico Basin at the east end of Red Rock Canyon. Of 27 climbs, 25 are trad and two are sport. Grades run from 5.8 into the 5.11s, with more than half at 5.8 and a spread of 5.10s above that. The face catches sun for the whole day, which keeps it comfortable on cool days. The walk goes up a trail and then a loose rocky slope toward a pinkish face. The multi-pitch Classic Crack of Calico, a popular moderate, is the headline nearby.
